user.name: Jackson Stark
user.backstory: Jackson, Charley and Lily are having a late study session at the library, when the Wi-Fi goes down. Lily panics: "Can we still work without GitHub?" Time to find out why Git says yes.

cards.title: Two ways to share a project
body: Centralized: one central server holds the history. Everyone's laptop only has the latest files. Older tools like Subversion (SVN) work this way.
Distributed: every copy has the full history. Git works this way.
cards.diagram:
Centralized:   [laptop]   [laptop]   [laptop]
                     \        |        /
               [ Server: the only history ]

Distributed:   [laptop: full history] <--> [GitHub: full history] <--> [laptop: full history]

cards.title: You already have everything
body: When you clone a project, you get every snapshot ever made, not just the latest files. That's why `git log`, `git commit`, `git branch` and `git switch` all work with no internet.

cards.title: Only some commands need internet
body: The commands that talk to GitHub need internet: `git clone`, `git push` and `git pull`. Everything else works anywhere, even on a plane.

cards.title: No single point of failure
body: In a centralized system, if the server breaks, the history can be lost. With Git, every clone is a full backup. GitHub is just the copy your team agreed to share. That's what "distributed" means.

questions.prompt: What's the big difference between centralized and distributed version control?
options: In distributed (like Git), every copy has the full history
questions.wrongFeedback: In a distributed system like Git, every copy has the full history. In a centralized one, only the server does.

questions.prompt: No Wi-Fi, so the push failed. But Jackson can still save new work. Commit the staged changes with the message on the profile card.

startingHistory.text: fatal: unable to access 'https://github.com/charley-dunkel-gitlingo/weather-app.git/': Could not resolve host: github.com

questions.prompt: The Wi-Fi is still down. Which of these commands won't work?
questions.wrongFeedback: `git push` talks to GitHub, so it needs internet. `git commit` and `git log` only use your own copy.

questions.prompt: Imagine GitHub's copy of the weather app was lost. Could the team get their project back?
options: No, GitHub had the only history
Yes, any teammate's clone has the full history
Only the latest files, not the history
questions.wrongFeedback: Every clone is a full copy of the history, so any teammate could put it all back.
